newsitem.title: UK: BSkyB orders one million digital TV boxes.
newsitem.headline: BSkyB orders one million digital TV boxes.

text.p: British Sky Broadcasting Plc said on Tuesday it had placed orders for one million set top boxes as part of its drive into digital television.
BSkyB has joined forces with British Telecommunications Plc, Midland Bank and Matsushita Electric in a new company to deliver digital interactive services to television viewers in the UK.
BT and BSkyB will each have a 32.5 percent stake in the new company, British Interactive Broadcasting Limited (BIB). Midland will take a 20 percent stake and Matsushita the remaining 15 percent.

The shareholders have agreed pro-rata funding of 265 million pounds($433.3 million) to establish the infrastructure for the new services and subsidise the digital satellite boxes. The subsidy will allow the boxes to retail at about 200 pounds.
BIB will enable high street businesses to offer interactive services including home shopping and banking to television viewers.

BIB expects its services to be available from the summer of 1998 following the launch of BSkyB's digital broadcast service next spring. BSkyB also announced pre-tax profits of 215 million pounds for the nine months to end-March, a 21 percent rise.($ = 0.611 British Pounds)
